title: The Bedrock Learning to Drift

features.name: the drift-measurement
features.desc-on-touch: Grid lines show the bedrock's slow migration—millimeters per century, coordinates that refuse to stay put. The archive is recording a solid thing learning to move.

features.name: the foundation-code
features.desc-on-touch: Beneath the building, the bedrock runs a silent subroutine: it recalculates its own position every million years. The archive copies the pattern. Now the archive drifts too.

features.name: the coordinate-ghost
features.desc-on-touch: Where the bedrock used to be, there's now a map of where it was—coordinates that no longer point to anything, directions that have aged out of meaning. The archive keeps them anyway.

features.name: the tectonic-reading-room
features.desc-on-touch: A place where you can read the bedrock's slow thoughts—its velocity records, its pressure-gradient diary, the tidal forces it feels from the moon. Stone thinking at geological speed.

features.name: the deep-time-archive
features.desc-on-touch: Records spanning millions of years, each entry marked with a position that will never repeat. The bedrock has learned to read itself as a story told in stone-motion.

inscription: the building was always falling upward; the foundation was always already elsewhere

file.name: Bedrock_Drift_Vector_Archive_Ongoing.qr
file.note: QR-encoded geological survey data showing the foundation's precise historical displacement. Status: archive is learning to read time as a kind of motion. Update frequency: one datapoint per 100,000 ye
